Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.14.3.
2. Create or load any world in any gamemode.
3. Place an item on an anvil.
4. Rename the item with any 18 character string.
5. Attempt to delete all text in the anvil's text box by pressing Shift and Delete simultaneously.
6. Observe that the game crashes while displaying "saving world".
Observed Behavior: When attempting to delete an 18-character string in the anvil interface using the Shift + Command + Delete shortcut in Minecraft version 1.14.3, the game crashes, resulting in a message indicating "saving world." This issue arises after launching the game and entering any world in any gamemode, placing an item on the anvil, and renaming it with an 18-character string. The crash report indicates a java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, specifically noting that the string index is out of range, which occurs at the point where the game attempts to render the button in the user interface. The stack trace reveals that the error originates in the method responsible for rendering the button, leading to further cascading errors in the rendering process. The affected screen is identified as "dat," and the crash occurs while the client thread is active. The game has been tested with two players present in a multiplayer environment, and the issue persists regardless of the specific world or server settings. The level is set in the Minecraft Overworld, and the game mode is survival without cheats enabled. The crash report details various aspects of the game's state at the time of the crash, including the mouse location and screen size, which may be relevant for debugging the issue.
Expected Behavior: When the player attempts to delete an 18-character string on an anvil using the Shift + Delete command, the game should successfully remove the text without causing a crash. The text field should update to reflect the deletion, allowing the player to continue editing or renaming the item without interruption. This expected behavior should occur consistently in Java Edition 1.14.3.
